_note: SBEG 46X Lab 11 -- simulated powered wheelchair in a hospital ward. ILLUSTRATIVE VALUES (teaching values, not the data of a real product). Units: m, rad, s. Chassis configuration q = (phi, x, y) as in Modern Robotics Ch. 13; {b} at the midpoint of the drive-wheel axle, x_b forward.

chair._comment: nominal model used by odometry, EKF and controller: drive-wheel radius r, half the distance between the drive wheels d (track 2d = 0.56 m), wheel speed limit u_max (rad/s), indoor speed limit v_max (m/s), wheel encoders (counts per wheel revolution), control/odometry period h

truth._comment: the simulated chair (unknown to the filter): effective wheel radii and half-track (tyre compression, wear), and random slip: each wheel's ground distance per step has variance k_slip * |r Delta theta| (m^2)

sensor._comment: range-bearing sensor at the origin of {b} (lidar + retro-reflective ID markers): one scan every 'every' samples (0.2 s), every marker closer than max_range is detected with its ID; a fraction p_outlier of readings is a reflection (range too short by U(0.5, 1.5) m)

ekf._comment: filter model: wheel distance noise variance k_s |r Delta theta| per wheel and step (m^2); sensor noise; initial standard deviations (2 deg, 2 cm, 2 cm) at the docking station; Mahalanobis gate = chi-square 99 % with 2 DOF

route._comment: ward loop around the nurses' station: straight 6 m, left turn of radius 1.5 m, straight 4 m, ... (29.42 m per lap) at 0.6 m/s

control._comment: gains of the nonlinear tracking law (MR Eq. 13.31; k1 in 1/m, k2 in 1/m^2, k3 in 1/m), reference point x_r and gain k_p of the point-tracking law (MR Eqs. 13.21, 13.29), initial pose error of the closed-loop runs

arm_mount._comment: optional Part D: srs_7r_feeding base frame {0} in the chair frame {b} (right armrest, no rotation) and a feeding pose
